title: Drift Wood #9 · the Rain
logline: January. Wood explains Bresson to a cashier. The rain explains nothing.

panels.composition: The grocery on 101 in January. Rain in vertical hatching across the whole panel. WOOD at the register with one item: a can of soup.

characters.pose: at the register, soup in hand

image.prompt: a small-town grocery checkout in January, rain drawn as frantic vertical hatching in the windows, a teenage boy in an overcoat holding a single can of soup, a bored cashier

balloons.text: Bresson said a film should express itself through the rhythm of images and sounds. Not acting. Never acting. Do you know what that means for a town like this?

image.prompt: a teenage boy leaning on a checkout counter earnestly explaining something to a gum-chewing cashier
close-up of a bored teenage cashier chewing gum, flat expression

panels.composition: Outside. Wood under the awning with his soup, the rain doing exactly what Bresson would have wanted. He watches it for a whole panel.

characters.pose: under an awning, soup bag in hand, watching rain

image.prompt: a teenage boy standing under a grocery awning holding a small bag, watching heavy rain fall in vertical hatching across an empty parking lot, no words

notes: The first Rain. Silent last panel — the seed of every landscape.
